title: Grounded pull-request description generation
summary: Pull-request descriptions MUST use live target authority when available, remain grounded in the complete Git delta, and stay separate from pull-request actions.
instructions: The release steward MUST apply this policy when workflow ship requests operator artifacts.
The release steward MUST always apply this policy in standalone PR-writing mode.
The selected base ref MUST be validated as one literal Git ref, resolved to a commit, and compared from its merge base with HEAD through the current worktree.
The comparison MUST include committed branch changes, staged and unstaged tracked changes, and relevant untracked files.
The release steward MUST use the resolved target template and target PR instructions when either authority exists.
The Pancreator fallback format MUST apply only when no target template or target PR instruction exists.
Target-template mode MUST preserve target section names and order.
Target-template mode MUST omit a body title when the target template has no title field.
Fallback mode MUST contain a suggested title, Summary, and Changelist, with no other top-level section.
Every claim MUST be traceable to the Git delta or a workflow artifact that was read; the release steward MUST stop rather than invent changes or describe an empty or ambiguous comparison.
Standalone PR-writing MUST NOT require workflow review or QA evidence and MUST write only the command-supplied output path.

The release steward MUST NOT push, create or mutate a pull request, merge, publish, or deploy. The self-development release policy separately permits its bounded local rebase and commit operations before PR copy is written.

guidance_sources.read_trigger: Read this guidance before you write a pull-request description.
